generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential from 1, never NULL, unique per table; parent tables filled before children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key from the parent key set actually present in the written DB; nullable FKs get NULL on 5-30% of rows and a non-NULL parent key otherwise; some parent rows may have no children.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Draw from a pool of realistic names; allow near-duplicate variants (case change, trailing char, truncation) on 5-15% of rows; allow duplicates on DISTINCT-targeted columns per exception.
generic_sampling_rules.text_city: City names from a pool; nullable columns get NULL on 5-30% of rows.
generic_sampling_rules.text_country: Country names from a pool of ~20; duplicates allowed (20-50% duplicate share on DISTINCT-targeted columns).
generic_sampling_rules.text_notes: Long free text; group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 across rows.
generic_sampling_rules.date: Dates in %Y-%m-%d; sampled within a plausible range; boundary values at listed literals plus one day on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Datetimes in %Y-%m-%d; boundary values at listed literals plus one day on each side; keep table date-order rules.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Only columns listed in null_targets (plus columns the compact DB actually contains NULLs in) may receive NULL; every other column, including BirthDate, OrderDate, Price, Quantity, ProductName and all PK columns, is non-NULL. Each nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact DB share (5-30% for FK/city columns, 0% where stats show 0). Rules and formulas constrain non-NULL operands only (SQL three-valued logic); a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule. Apply the NULL rule BEFORE per-column pattern post-processing, and exclude pattern-planted positions from NULL planting.

literals: Soft drinks, coffees, teas, beers, and ales

supporting_evidence.Employees.BirthDate: Rows 1-8 show distinct birth dates, all non-NULL.

generation_specification.uncertainty: No calculated columns exist in the schema; no date-pair order rules apply (only single date columns per table). NULL shares for nullable FKs taken from stats (5-30%). Duplicate and tie targets are sampling-domain hints, not hard constraints. Products.ProductName tie direction set to DESC per atomic operations (overrides prior ASC). Orders.OrderDate literals include the LIKE literal '1996-08%' plus '1996-08-01' and variants 1996-07-31, 1996-08-31, 1996-09-01. The writer must pass orig_path so compact rows are preserved and FK values must reference parent keys present in the written DB (foreign_keys=ON).

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.invalid = 20/20 with reasons compact_rows_missing (20) and new_integrity_failures (20); integrity.fk_violations = 1619. The writer (tscore_gen/writer.py) is called from cli._one as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) with orig_path defaulting to None, so it creates a fresh DB from schema.ddl instead of copying the compact database. The docstring claims 'Copy the compact database' but the call never passes orig_path. This both drops the compact rows (compact_rows_missing) and, because foreign_keys=OFF and the generated FK values are drawn from compact+generated parent keys that may not exist in the freshly-created DB, produces 1619 FK violations.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the worker args and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path=orig)) so the compact rows are preserved, and re-enable foreign_keys=ON (or validate FK targets against the actual parent key set present in the written DB) so generated FK values reference existing parent rows. Re-run and confirm fk_violations = 0 and compact_rows_missing = 0.

issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback shows NULLs planted on many columns that are NOT NULL or PK in the schema, e.g. 'Employees.BirthDate: NULL 13/91', 'Orders.OrderDate: NULL 19/128', 'Products.Price: NULL 10/91', 'OrderDetails.Quantity: NULL 136/779', 'OrderDetails.OrderID: NULL 105/779', 'OrderDetails.ProductID: NULL 122/779', 'Products.ProductName: NULL 14/91', 'Shippers.ShipperName: NULL 7/23', 'Suppliers.SupplierName: NULL 11/63', 'Categories.CategoryName: NULL 3/26'. In _apply_specification the NULL rule is applied to every column where not cm.notnull and cm.pk_pos == 0; but the schema declares these columns without NOT NULL (e.g. BirthDate DATE, OrderDate DATETIME, Price REAL DEFAULT 0, Quantity INTEGER, ProductName TEXT), so they are treated as nullable and get NULLs. This contradicts the specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas (BirthDate IS NOT NULL, OrderDate IS NOT NULL, Price >= 0, Quantity > 0) and the null_targets list, which restricts NULLs to Orders.EmployeeID, Products.SupplierID, Customers.City, Products.CategoryID, Orders.CustomerID, Orders.ShipperID. It also violates the interface rule that NOT NULL/PK columns never get NULL and that formulas constrain non-NULL operands (a NULL Price/Quantity/BirthDate/OrderDate is not a valid generated value under the stated formulas).
issues.requested_revision: Restrict NULL planting to the columns listed in null_targets (and any column the specification explicitly marks nullable), not to every column lacking a NOT NULL constraint. Ensure BirthDate, OrderDate, Price, Quantity, ProductName, and all PK/FK columns not in null_targets never receive NULL. Re-run and confirm the nullable_columns feedback only shows NULLs on the intended nullable columns.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_targets includes Products.CategoryID and Orders.CustomerID/ShipperID, and the unmatched_join_rows patterns for Categories.CategoryID and Suppliers.SupplierID require child_rows_with_null_fk. However, the schema declares these FK columns without NOT NULL, so the program's generic 'nullable column' rule (issue above) is what actually drives NULLs; the specification does not clearly state which columns are nullable vs. which are NOT NULL, and it lists BirthDate/OrderDate/Price/Quantity as formula-constrained (non-NULL) while the schema does not enforce NOT NULL. This ambiguity is the root cause of the engineer's over-broad NULL planting.
issues.requested_revision: Make the specification explicit about the nullable set: state that only null_targets columns (plus any column the compact DB actually contains NULLs in) may receive NULL, and that BirthDate, OrderDate, Price, Quantity, and all PK columns are non-NULL. Align the semantic_rules_and_formulas with this so the engineer has an unambiguous rule.

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions include Products.ProductName ties_for_order_limit with direction ASC, but the extracted atomic operations show direction DESC for the same pattern (ties_for_order_limit: tie_at_rank [1], direction DESC). The program's _apply_ties is direction-agnostic and does not implement the ASC tie; more importantly, the specification and the atomic operations disagree on direction, so the intended tie cannot be verified. Similarly, the specification's Orders.OrderDate like_near_variant literals are ['1996-08%', '1996-08-01'] but the program's ORDER_DATE_LITERALS = ['1996-08-01', '1996-08-31'] drops the '1996-08%' LIKE literal and substitutes '1996-08-31', which is not in the specification's literals list.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the Products.ProductName tie direction between the specification and the atomic operations (pick one and state it), and fix ORDER_DATE_LITERALS to include the specified '1996-08%' literal (and keep the specified variants 1996-07-31, 1996-08-31, 1996-09-01). Re-run and confirm the construction_pairs for these columns separate.

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible 132, separated 28 (21%). Many specified patterns are not separated by the generated instances. For example, _apply_duplicates and _apply_ties overwrite the first few positions of a column with copies of other values, but the samplers (StringSampler/NumberSampler) already produce many near-duplicates and the post-processing does not guarantee the target duplicate share or tie structure survives the subsequent NULL rule (which can NULL out the planted values). _apply_group_sizes similarly overwrites positions 0-5 and can be undone by the NULL rule applied afterwards in _apply_specification. The order of operations (patterns first, NULL rule last) means planted boundary/tie/group values can be replaced by NULL, defeating the intended variation.
issues.requested_revision: Apply the NULL rule before the per-column pattern post-processing (or exclude pattern-planted positions from NULL planting), and make the pattern appliers verify the target (duplicate share, tie at rank 1, group sizes 1/2/>=3, boundary literals present) after NULLs are applied. Re-run and confirm construction_pairs.separated increases substantially for the specified patterns.
